text: Confirmed: in tree.go's `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` (used by RedirectFixedPath) the code descends with `n = n.children[0]` and then switches on the node type, assuming the wildcard child is first — but wildcard children are always stored LAST (`addChild` inserts static children before the wildcard, and getValue uses `children[len(children)-1]`). So for a node with both `/prefix/xxx` and `/prefix/:id`, children[0] is the static node and the switch hits `default: panic("invalid node type")`. Fixing: use the last child, and try static children case-insensitively first (so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to /prefix/xxx) with the wildcard only as fallback (so /prefix/a/b/c 404s). ETA ~5 min.

Confirmed: `NegotiateFormat` iterates `for ; i < len(accepted); i++` but indexes `offer[i]` too, so when the Accept entry is longer than the offered format (e.g. accepted "image/tiff-fx" vs offer "image/tiff") it indexes past the end of the offer → `index out of range [10] with length 10`. Fix: bound the loop by the offer length as well, so a longer Accept entry simply doesn't match and "" is returned. ETA ~5 min.

Confirmed: `Context.FileAttachment` writes the ASCII filename into `Content-Disposition` verbatim (`attachment; filename="`+filename+`"`), so embedded `"`/`\` break out of the quoted string and inject extra header parameters. Fix: escape `\` and `"` in the filename (the same escaping net/http uses) so the header always holds exactly one well-formed filename. ETA ~5 min.
